result_text:
Suppliers now carry payment terms in days. A new supplier defaults to 30, and the four listings you named show the stored value. The full suite passes: 176 test classes, no failures or errors. I did not commit.

What changed:

- **`schema.sql`**: `supplier` gets `payment_terms_days INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 30`, with a check that it is not negative.
- **`model/Supplier.java`**: new `paymentTermsDays` component, plus a `STANDARD_PAYMENT_TERMS_DAYS = 30` constant. The existing 5-argument constructor is kept and defaults to 30, so the roughly 100 existing call sites compile unchanged.
- **`DataStore.java`**: `createSupplier` and `updateSupplier` write the terms. `listSuppliersByName`, `listSuppliersByCountry`, `listSuppliersByMinimumRating` and `findSupplierById` read them.
- **`SupplierTest.java`**: three new tests. One covers the Swedish supplier registered at 45 and renegotiated to 14, checked in all four listings. One checks the 30-day default. One checks that negative terms are rejected.

Decision for you: other `DataStore` queries that also build `Supplier` objects (reorder suggestions, purchased quantity per supplier, supplier performance and spending) still use the 5-argument constructor. They will therefore report 30 days regardless of what was agreed. I left them alone because the request named only the four listings. Say if you want those queries to return the real terms too.
